findingSchema.path: path relative to the analysis root
findingSchema.line: 1-based integer, 0 when the finding is file- or project-scoped
findingSchema.evidence: the smallest source excerpt that proves the finding
findingSchema.fingerprint: sha256 of the finding identity; required for waiver matching

categories.D: Dependency and structure: what may reference what

thirdPartyTiers.declaration: externals map in acima.config.json; tiers are declared per package and never inferred

tiers.platform: Runtime, framework or hosting surface. Banned from contracts, no adapter required.
tiers.integration: IO, state, wire format or a third-party surface. Exactly one adapter unit and one port unit per vendor.
tiers.utility: Pure and dependency-free at the API surface. Free inside implementations; none of its types may cross a contract or port.

roles.adapter: Holds one declared vendor package; implements the port; translates vendor types and failures.
roles.port: Dependency-free contracts unit declaring the capability in the service's own vocabulary.

rules.title: Implementation references another implementation
rules.summary: A module implementation may never reference, import or link another module's implementation.
rules.fix: Import the provider's contracts port; if it lacks the operation you need, request an additive contract change from its owner instead of referencing the implementation.

rules.title: Contracts reference an implementation
rules.summary: A contracts unit must not depend on any implementation unit, including its own.
rules.fix: Define the contract shape independently and map to it inside the implementation, which already knows both types.

rules.title: Contracts reference another contracts unit
rules.summary: Contracts must be independently consumable. Declare local value types or carry identity instead of importing another contracts unit.
rules.fix: Declare a local value type in this contracts unit, carry identity (ids and primitives), or duplicate the shape; never reference another contracts unit.

rules.title: Contracts carry a third-party dependency
rules.summary: Contracts may depend only on the language's core library. Third-party packages and framework types belong in implementations or adapters.
rules.fix: Replace validation attributes with constructor checks and move serializer concerns to a transport type at the composition boundary; contracts keep only the language's core library.

rules.title: Circular module dependency
rules.summary: The module dependency graph must be acyclic.
rules.fix: Break the cycle in order of preference: a process manager that owns the workflow, an event replacing one direction, or a merge if both are one bounded context; never route the shared type through the kernel.

rules.title: Contracts reference a composition boundary
rules.summary: Contracts must not know how they are assembled, hosted, wired or deployed.
rules.fix: Remove the reference and pass what the handler needs as a contract member, or resolve it inside the implementation through a consumer-owned port.

rules.title: Shared kernel violation
rules.summary: The shared kernel may hold only dependency-free value types; it must not reference modules or carry behaviour.
rules.fix: Move the type to the owning module or to the contract project that needs it, and keep only dependency-free values in the kernel.

rules.title: Transitive implementation leak
rules.summary: A reference must not deliver another module's implementation transitively.
rules.fix: Remove the reference that creates the leak: PrivateAssets="all" on implementation-internal references in .NET, no impl re-export from the contracts entry point in TypeScript, internal/ or JPMS exports elsewhere.

rules.title: Access to another module's internals
rules.summary: Non-contract types of a module must not be reachable from outside it.
rules.fix: Ask the owner for a view through a provided port; if none exists, declare your own port and adapt rather than importing the owner's model.

rules.title: Domain references infrastructure
rules.summary: A module's domain and application logic must not depend on its infrastructure or delivery mechanisms.
rules.fix: Declare the port in the application layer, implement it in infrastructure, and inject it so dependencies point inward.

rules.title: Contracts reference a framework type
rules.summary: Contracts must not expose hosting, transport, ORM or serialization framework types.
rules.fix: Keep the message about the business and move transport or hosting concerns into the handler, or into an explicit envelope type in the host.

rules.title: Implementation type published outside the module
rules.summary: Only contracts types may be public outside a module.
rules.fix: Make the type internal, unexported or package-private, and move anything that genuinely crosses the boundary into the contracts unit.

rules.title: Module resolved through a service locator
rules.summary: Modules must declare their dependencies explicitly; resolving peers at runtime hides coupling.
rules.fix: Take the port as a constructor parameter; resolving a peer module at runtime hides a boundary crossing the dependency graph cannot see.
rules.manualEvidence: Inspect construction and container resolution for service-locator or runtime peer resolution; record every composition path.

rules.title: Mutable contract state
rules.summary: Contract members are set at construction and never mutated afterwards.
rules.fix: Make it immutable: C# sealed record with init members, TypeScript readonly members, Python frozen dataclass or NamedTuple, Go unexported fields with accessors, Java record.

rules.title: Mutable collection exposure
rules.summary: Contracts expose immutable or defensively copied collections, never shared mutable state.
rules.fix: Expose a read-only collection: IReadOnlyList<T> from ToArray(), readonly T[] or ReadonlyArray, tuple[T, ...] or MappingProxyType, an accessor returning a copy, or List.copyOf.

rules.title: Behaviour in contracts
rules.summary: Contracts carry data and validation only; no business logic, IO or orchestration.
rules.fix: Keep at most a pure fold in the contract; move anything that branches on business conditions, does IO or is async into the module, and compute what consumers need there.
rules.manualEvidence: Review every contract type for business behaviour, IO, orchestration and lifecycle hooks; record the reviewed units.

rules.title: Ambient or non-deterministic state in contracts
rules.summary: Contracts must not read clocks, generate identifiers, or touch static mutable state.
rules.fix: Take time and identity as constructor parameters supplied by the module that owns the fact; the clock belongs in the implementation.

rules.title: Persistence type leak
rules.summary: Contracts must not expose entities, sessions, queryables or database types.
rules.fix: Make a query a request with typed parameters and a view a flat immutable projection built by the module; never expose entities, sessions or queryables.

rules.title: Untyped payload
rules.summary: Contracts must be explicitly typed; object, dynamic, any or bare dictionaries are not contracts.
rules.fix: Declare one typed contract per event and keep any generic transport envelope in the host.

rules.title: Contract cannot be constructed in one step
rules.summary: A contract type must make its required state obvious and constructible atomically.
rules.fix: Put required values in the constructor, make optional values explicit, and use a builder in the implementation only when construction is genuinely staged.
rules.manualEvidence: Review every contract type for one-step construction and obvious required state; record builders and exceptions.

rules.title: Opaque business behavior
rules.summary: A published contract or operation must make the business outcome it serves visible: its preconditions, failure semantics and observable effects.
rules.fix: Document the business decision, required preconditions, failure modes and visible effects on the contract or API; keep implementation logic out of the contract.
rules.manualEvidence: Review every published contract and operation for the business outcome, preconditions, failure semantics and visible effects; record the reviewed surfaces and the answer.

rules.title: Shared database ownership
rules.summary: Each module owns its persistence; no other module reads or writes its schema.
rules.fix: Call the owner's port for reads and subscribe to its events for data you keep in your own schema; never read another module's tables, even read-only.

rules.title: Cross-module configuration key
rules.summary: A module must not read another module's configuration keys.
rules.fix: Move the key under your own namespace, supplied by the host; if the value belongs to the provider, ask for it through a port.
rules.manualEvidence: Review configuration keys and secrets for cross-module access; record each module namespace.

rules.title: Cross-module mutable static state
rules.summary: Modules must not communicate through shared mutable statics.
rules.fix: Make the cache an instance owned by the module and inject it; if several modules need the same data, the host constructs one instance and passes it.

rules.title: Version-lock coupling
rules.summary: Consumers depend on a contracts version range, never on an implementation version.
rules.fix: Depend on X.Contracts with a version range; needing the implementation's version means D001 is still present.
rules.manualEvidence: Review published package and artifact version edges; record contracts ranges and implementation pins.

rules.title: Configuration read outside the composition boundary
rules.summary: A module-owned component must not read deployment, operational or secret configuration from ambient environment variables or a global configuration object.
rules.fix: Resolve the value once at a composition boundary and pass it into the component constructor or composition function; the component should receive a value, not discover one.

rules.title: Meaningful value without one immutable owner
rules.summary: A meaningful primitive value must have one identifiable, immutable declaration at its highest appropriate ownership boundary; its semantic identity comes from what it represents, not its literal value or identifier alone, and shared or configuration values must be supplied explicitly.
rules.fix: Name the value once in the scope that genuinely owns its meaning, make the declaration immutable where the language supports it, and keep distinct policies separate; classify operationally variable values as explicit deployment or runtime configuration rather than mutable source state.
rules.automationNotes: Deterministic candidate detection covers inline literals, mutable declarations, same-module duplicate declarations and configuration/secret-looking names. Semantic equivalence, common ownership and the correct configuration category require review; Go, .NET and Java report this rule executed:false and require manual evidence.

rules.title: Undocumented exception
rules.summary: Every waiver carries an owner, a reason, a scope and an expiry date; every waiver carries the exact finding fingerprint.
rules.fix: Write owner, reason, scope, fingerprint, reviewedOn and expires; if you cannot name an owner or a date, the exception is not a decision yet.

rules.title: Expired waiver
rules.summary: An expired waiver is a violation until it is renewed or removed.
rules.fix: Fix the code, or renew the waiver individually with a fresh reason and expiry — never in bulk.

rules.title: Undocumented contract surface
rules.summary: Every public contract type documents its meaning and its invariants.
rules.fix: Document what the type means and what must be true: units, invariants, idempotency and failure semantics; one or two sentences is enough.

rules.title: Unreviewed contract change
rules.summary: A change to a published contracts surface must be captured in the versioned API baseline.
rules.fix: Make the change additive, or regenerate acima/evidence/api-surface.json in the same commit and mark the release as breaking.
rules.manualEvidence: Compare the contracts surface with the reviewed API baseline; record additive and breaking changes.

rules.title: Unclassified source
rules.summary: Every production source file belongs to a declared unit; a file outside every unit fails the run.
rules.fix: Declare the unit with a role and a module name, or add an exclusion with a reason; a repository that classifies nothing is a false pass.

rules.title: Port exposes a vendor shape
rules.summary: A port unit is dependency-free: it imports no third-party package and names no vendor type, so consumers never inherit the vendor.
rules.fix: Describe the capability in the port's own vocabulary (handles, requests, results) and move every vendor import and vendor type into the adapter that implements the port.

rules.title: Integration library used outside its declared adapter
rules.summary: A package declared with tier integration is imported only by its declared adapter unit; every other unit reaches the capability through the port.
rules.fix: Move the import into the adapter declared in externals, or declare the package with the tier it really has; the rest of the system takes the port and never the vendor.

rules.title: Adapter without a port
rules.summary: Every adapter unit is declared in externals with exactly one port unit, and every integration entry names both.
rules.fix: Declare the port unit and the externals entry (adapter and port), or delete the adapter: an adapter with no port is an unguarded vendor import with a new directory name.

rules.title: Vendor type outside the adapter
rules.summary: A vendor type appears in a signature, field or export outside the adapter unit.
rules.fix: Map the vendor type to the port's own type inside the adapter; application, domain, contracts and host code must never name a vendor type.

rules.title: Undeclared external dependency
rules.summary: Every package in a declared manifest has an externals entry with tier, owner, reason, review date and expiry, and no entry is past its review date.
rules.fix: Run acima.py externals --write-draft, then assign the tier, owner and reason for each package; renew or remove an entry whose review date has passed.

rules.title: Optional construction dependency
rules.summary: A module-owned constructor requires every input the component needs; an optional or defaulted parameter is a second construction path with hidden behaviour.
rules.fix: Require the parameter at every construction site and pass it from a composition boundary; if the behaviour is genuinely optional, model it explicitly with a named policy or a documented no-op implementation instead of an omitted argument.

rules.title: Optional argument hides an operational decision
rules.summary: A module-owned method or function does not use an optional or defaulted parameter to hide a decision its caller should make.
rules.fix: Require the argument, or split the operation into distinct methods, or take an explicit options value whose fields are required; keep a default only where a language or framework contract needs it, and document why.

rules.title: Implicit component registration
rules.summary: Module-owned components must be registered and constructed explicitly at a composition boundary; automatic scanning, convention registration and dynamic discovery must not hide the graph.
rules.fix: Register each component explicitly and construct it with named dependencies; if a framework scanner is unavoidable, declare a reviewed exception and prove the discovered set.

rules.title: Property or field injection
rules.summary: A module-owned component must receive dependencies through its constructor or composition function, not through property or field injection or post-construction assignment.
rules.fix: Move the dependency to the constructor and supply it at a composition boundary; if activation is framework-managed, keep the required dependencies in the declared constructor.

rules.title: Closed-over module-owned dependency
rules.summary: A module-owned component must receive module-owned collaborators through declared parameters or fields; it must not capture them from an enclosing scope through a closure, returned function or callback.
rules.fix: Pass the collaborator as a parameter or constructor field, or bind it explicitly at the composition boundary; keep closures for pure values and transformations.

rules.title: Partial application of a module-owned dependency
rules.summary: Partial application or method binding of a module-owned dependency must occur at a composition boundary; a component must not pre-bind a collaborator into a function it returns.
rules.fix: Move the partial application to the composition boundary and pass the resulting function in, or keep every dependency as an explicit parameter of the component's function.

rules.title: Unlabeled function or method argument
rules.summary: When the language supports named arguments, every statically resolved argument passed to a module-owned function or method uses the receiving parameter's name at the call site.
rules.fix: Use the language's native named-argument syntax for each supplied value, such as create_order(request_id=request_id, customer_id=wrong_variable) in Python or CreateOrder(requestId: requestId, customerId: wrongVariable) in C#. Do not invent wrapper objects to simulate named arguments in languages without native syntax.
rules.automationNotes: Implemented for Python and C# where native named-call syntax exists. Static analysis checks locally declared module-owned callables whose signatures can be resolved. TypeScript/JavaScript and Go have no native named-argument call syntax, so their enforcers report executed:false rather than inventing syntax or requiring wrapper objects. Unresolved external, reflective and dynamic call targets remain outside the deterministic subset.

rules.title: Unnecessary transient lifetime
rules.summary: A stateless shared service should be shared; a transient lifetime must be justified by independent identity, isolated mutable state, a short-lived resource or an operation boundary.
rules.fix: Register the stateless shared service at the longest appropriate lifetime (system/process/shared) rather than transient; keep transient only for components whose identity or state requires it.

rules.title: Captive scoped dependency
rules.summary: A longer-lived component must not directly capture a dependency with a shorter lifecycle; use an explicit scope boundary or lifecycle-aware factory that does not conceal the dependency.
rules.fix: Shorten the consumer lifetime, move the dependency to the call surface, or use a reviewed factory/scope boundary that resolves the shorter-lived dependency at the correct time.

rules.title: Shared mutable state without ownership
rules.summary: A shared component must not contain incidental mutable state without an explicit owner, isolation boundary and, where concurrent access is possible, a synchronization or concurrency strategy.
rules.fix: Move the state to a repository, request/operation context, cache or state store with an explicit owner and lifecycle; make the shared service stateless, or document and enforce safe isolation and synchronization.

rules.title: Non-idiomatic type identifier
rules.summary: A user-defined class, interface, type alias or enum must follow the target language's established type-name convention; semantic naming quality is assessed separately.
rules.fix: Rename the type to the language's type convention (PascalCase in Python, TypeScript, C#, Go and Java), while preserving the domain term; do not rename framework, generated or external types.

rules.title: Generic responsibility name
rules.summary: A module-owned type must not use a generic placeholder such as Helper, Manager, Processor, Utility, Common, Base, Default or Generic as a substitute for its actual responsibility.
rules.fix: Name the responsibility or domain concept directly (OrderValidator, PriceCalculator, PaymentAuthorizer), or document why the generic role is the precise abstraction in this context.

rules.title: Semantic naming clarity review
rules.summary: Names must communicate responsibility, behaviour, side effects, domain meaning and relevant units; abbreviations, boolean polarity, contextual sufficiency and lifecycle/version naming require semantic review.
rules.fix: Rewrite the identifier in the domain's vocabulary: state the operation and outcome, make side effects explicit, name the unit, expand local abbreviations, use positive boolean conditions, and remove incidental lifecycle or version information from the identity.
rules.manualEvidence: Record the reviewed naming decision, the affected public or application surface, the rationale, and the reviewer for each repository scope.

rules.title: Unowned effect boundary
rules.summary: Every externally visible effect has exactly one owning module; the owner declares its trigger, commit boundary, retry owner, idempotency and compensation.
rules.fix: Assign one owner module and declare the effect's trigger, commit point, retry owner, idempotency or deduplication rule and compensation; route cross-module effects through that owner.
rules.manualEvidence: Maintain an effect inventory: owner module, trigger, commit boundary, retry owner, idempotency key, compensation and every cross-module effect call.

rules.title: Hidden effect semantics
rules.summary: A published operation or event makes its effect semantics visible: whether it writes, sends, publishes, deletes, charges or schedules, and how retry, idempotency and failure behave.
rules.fix: Declare the observable effect, retryability, idempotency and failure semantics on the operation or result type; do not hide a meaningful effect behind a data-only or read-named surface.
rules.manualEvidence: Review every published operation and event for caller-visible effect semantics: effect kind, retryability, idempotency, result and failure modes.

rules.title: Untruthful effect outcome
rules.summary: An operation reports success only after its owned effect is committed, and distinguishes failure, partial completion, cancellation and unknown outcome.
rules.fix: Report success after the commit point, return a typed failure, partial, cancelled or unknown outcome, reject unsafe duplicates and define compensation where recovery is possible.
rules.manualEvidence: Exercise success, duplicate, retry, timeout, cancellation, partial completion and unknown-outcome scenarios; record observed state, returned outcome and recovery action.

rules.title: Critical effect without evidence
rules.summary: Every critical effect emits owned, correlated evidence sufficient to establish what changed, for whom, under which operation and with what outcome.
rules.fix: Emit an owned audit or operational record with actor, subject, operation or correlation identity, outcome and timestamp; define retention, access and a tested failure case.
rules.manualEvidence: List critical effects and show the owned audit or operational record: actor, subject, operation or correlation id, outcome, timestamp, retention and access.

rules.title: Telemetry conceals or alters business behaviour
rules.summary: Logging, metrics and telemetry must observe application behaviour without concealing it, replacing a business decision or materially changing the outcome, and must distinguish operational diagnostics, business events and required audit records by owner and purpose.
rules.fix: Keep logging and telemetry at the observation boundary: log the outcome the business decision produced instead of computing it in the logger, never let a diagnostic write decide or suppress a business result, and record business events and required audit records as owned outputs rather than incidental log lines.
rules.manualEvidence: Review every logging, metric, trace and telemetry call adjacent to a business decision: record what it observes, what it could conceal or replace, whether failing to emit changes behaviour, and whether a business event or required audit record is being served by a diagnostic log.

rules.title: Unowned consistency boundary
rules.summary: A multi-step state change or transaction must have exactly one identifiable owner and a declared consistency guarantee on return; atomicity is one strategy, not a universal requirement.
rules.fix: Name the component that owns the consistency boundary, state whether the operation is atomic, recoverable, compensating or reconciled, and document the intermediate states and the recovery, compensation or reconciliation path; do not let callers or the host own a boundary that belongs to the module.
rules.manualEvidence: For every multi-step state change and transaction, record the owning component, the guarantee on return, the intermediate states a caller can observe, and the recovery, compensation or reconciliation path with its owner.

fullRequires: every rule required by the declared level executed by its designated enforcement mechanism or covered by accepted, current, repository-scoped manual evidence
